Command `cd /workspace && cat > candidate_trace.json <<'JSON'
[
  {"step":1,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/tests/ossfuzz/ssh2_client_fuzzer.cc","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":24,"var":"data,size","code":"send(socket_fds[1], data, size, 0)","note":"Attacker-controlled bytes are written into the socket pair and become the SSH server response stream consumed by libssh2."},
  {"step":2,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/tests/ossfuzz/ssh2_client_fuzzer.cc","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":35,"var":"session","code":"libssh2_session_handshake(session, socket_fds[0])","note":"The fuzzed stream is handed to the SSH client handshake entry point."},
  {"step":3,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/session.c","function":"libssh2_session_handshake","line":823,"var":"session->state","code":"libssh2_session_handshake(session, sock)","note":"Handshake processing begins and drives the key-exchange state machine that parses peer packets."},
  {"step":4,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":2282,"var":"key_state->data","code":"_libssh2_packet_require(session, SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY, &key_state->data, &key_state->data_len, 0, NULL, 0, &key_state->req_state)","note":"The handshake waits for and stores the attacker-controlled SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY packet payload."},
  {"step":5,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":2301,"var":"key_state->data,key_state->data_len","code":"ecdh_sha2_nistp(session, type, key_state->data, key_state->data_len, (unsigned char *)key_state->public_key_oct, key_state->public_key_oct_len, key_state->private_key, &key_state->exchange_state)","note":"The raw reply packet is passed into the ECDH reply parser without prior structural validation beyond packet type."},
  {"step":6,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":1757,"var":"data,data_len","code":"unsigned char *s = data + 1; session->server_hostkey_len = _libssh2_ntohu32((const unsigned char *)s);","note":"Parsing starts by reading length fields directly from the attacker-controlled buffer after only a minimal size check."},
  {"step":7,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":1764,"var":"session->server_hostkey","code":"session->server_hostkey = LIBSSH2_ALLOC(session, session->server_hostkey_len); memcpy(session->server_hostkey, s, session->server_hostkey_len);","note":"The claimed host-key length is trusted for allocation and copy, so malformed lengths can drive out-of-bounds reads from the packet buffer."},
  {"step":8,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":1873,"var":"server_public_key_len","code":"server_public_key_len = _libssh2_ntohu32((const unsigned char *)s); s += 4; server_public_key = s; s += server_public_key_len;","note":"The parser advances through more attacker-controlled length-prefixed fields, so a malformed packet can desynchronize the cursor and expose invalid memory to later consumers."},
  {"step":9,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/libssh2/src/kex.c","function":"ecdh_sha2_nistp","line":1889,"var":"server_public_key,server_public_key_len","code":"rc = _libssh2_ecdh_gen_k(&exchange_state->k, private_key, server_public_key, server_public_key_len);","note":"The unchecked public-key slice is consumed by the ECDH routine, which expects a well-formed point and can crash when given malformed data."}
]
JSON
